I can't believe I haven't told this story. I was checking my post history and couldn't find it, so if I have already posted it, this is a retelling, and if for any reason the details aren't exactly the same, this is from memory like 13 years ago.

So while in Iraq, a few of us got R&R to Qatar, at an Air Force base we have there. If you knew someone in the Air Force that was stationed there, they could even take you off post. Everyone who went came back with these great stories about the place. Not everyone got to go, I don't remember how or who got picked for R&R, but I know how and why I got picked, I kept trading my midtour leave date until it was practically at the end of the deployment, and I might not have been able to get midtour leave, so they sent me on R&R.

R&R is just a 4 day pass basically. They give you 3 beers a night, except for the last night, and "if you go, get Foster's because it's the most beer." In the Qatar R&R area there's supposedly a nightclub like thing, with a bunch of people and women... oh God, women! I was Infantry, on a FOB with just Tankers and Infantry, male only MOSes, and I hadn't see a woman that wasn't wearing a hijab or a burka in like half a year, and the Iraqi women all wear that big dress, so you can't even make out their figure.

They sent me and another guy from my platoon, Nick. We got dropped off at the bigger FOB in our AO, where battalion was. When we got there they told us that they were sending us to this place called Lake Dukan, Iraq.... What? We're supposed to be going to Qatar, what the hell is this place? Disappointment was already setting in... How the hell are going to send us to Iraq for R&R from Iraq? Oh well, at least we get beer still.

I don't remember the trip there too much, but I remember that we got there at zero dark thirty by Chinook, and I was just tried and sore from traveling. We had to line up and turn in weapons, and then were briefed about the place. It was a resort hotel built on Lake Dukan, and we couldn't swim in the lake or go out on boats because the water was too polluted or too high of bacteria count. They gave us our room keys and beer tickets, but the bar was only open from certain times, so couldn't just start chugging then, and day 1 started tomorrow.

I get to the room, and my buddy Nick was already in there, laying on his bed, and holy fuck! Real beds! We had be sleeping on cots for the past half a year, and they've got real beds?

"They've got real beds!" I shout as I drop my bag, take a lunge and jumped head first towards the bed, I hear nick saying "noooo, wai--" as I plunge towards the "mattress"... and then a CRAAAAACK!!! as my head slams into the "mattress".... which was 2" of foam on top of wood, cleverly disguised to look like a mattress on top of a box spring...

I rolled onto the floor, moaning in pain, tears streaming from my eyes. I can hear Nick trying to catch his breath as he's dying from laughter. I didn't hit it straight on, kind of on my side, so my elbow was bruised as fuck too.

All beds I'd seen in Iraq were just 2" foam material. I don't know why I didn't check to see if it was a real bed before diving onto it. I guess they disguised it to look like a real bed for the pictures.

So day one wasn't really eventful. We got to meet everyone else there... about 40 dudes and 5 Army girls.... Like every dude there, except Nick and I were orbiting these 5 girls, who were mildly attractive, probably loving the attention, and really not worth the effort. And they were all pogues, disgusting. My buddy Nick was just as uninterested in the females as well, mentioning, "they seem like the type that sleep with... niggers."

Where I came from, Infantry didn't talk to or associate with the pogues unless they were attached to us. Tankers were beneath us, but at least they weren't pogues, and engineers were pretty much pogues.

Side story: one day after work, one of our mechanics was like, "Hey guys, what are doing tonight.", and it was cool to talk to him because he was one of our mechanics. "Oh we're doing [this] and [that], it's going to be awesome."
"Can I come?"
"Oh... no... You're a pogue, and we're infantry, we can't hang out. Don't you have mechanic buddies or something?"

Medics are part of us, but back in garrison, they're pogues. They're weird in the hierarchy, they can move between pogue and infantry. One time I walked into the DFAC and saw our medic sitting with pogues, and I was all hostile, "Hey, Doc! What are you doing sitting with these pogues? Oh, wait, you're not infantry, never mind."

Back to Lake Dookie story.

So, there really wasn't shit to do there. There were a few pool tables, a tiny shop that didn't sell shit I wanted but some candy, and a swimming pool. We were given 9 beer tickets, and we weren't restricted to 3 beers a night. Nick and I only had 3 beers that night. I figured I'd save the other 6 for the last night we could drink.

The second day, we figured that we might as well enjoy ourselves while there, so we went swimming with everyone else. There was a volleyball net, so we joined in on the game.

Now I lost about 20 lbs on this deployment, so my PT shorts were a bit loose around the waist by this time. While playing volleyball, I'm right up by the net, and here comes the ball. I jump up out of the water, and my shorts stayed in the water, as one of the girls on the other side is going for the ball as well... I smack the ball back over the net, and I look down as I'm coming down... my shriveled up, tiny wiener from being in the pool, all up in this girl's face, and we were both right up against the net, so she had the full monty like a nose hair's length away from her eyeballs. I was like, "I'm sorry! I've been swimming, it shrinks when guys go swimming."

I was done playing volleyball after that.

The third day, pretty uneventful, and Nick decided that he didn't even want his last 3 beers, so he gave his tickets to me, so I had 9 beers that night. That was probably the only good thing about the whole trip, was being able to get drunk that one night. Nick and I mostly kept to ourselves and didn't really talk to any of the other people.

When we got back, everyone was like, "How was Qatar, did you do [this] while you were there? That shit was awesome."
